subject: Brightware Q3 launch — cohort lift quota handshake & forecast
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@brightware.com>, launchops@brightware.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Brightware Q3 launch — cohort lift quota handshake & forecast

Hi Alice / Launch Ops,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Brightware confirmed a staged cohort launch in the US for the week of Apr 6 (internal milestone). You've sent the updated traffic forecast — attaching v2 of the spreadsheet. Quick summary of the ask from your side:

- Short term quota bump to support a 72-hour warmup window with an initial 2.5x concurrent request spike (peak day),
- A temporary rate-addendum for the launch window (we'll need procurement/legal to sign), and
- Confirmed routing rules for fallback to a smaller model variant if latency or capacity issues occur.

Internal asks for the product/ops team:
- Karthik: what model variant would you recommend as the fallback and what KV-caching behavior should be enabled for the cohort?
- Marcus: can infra open a temporary rate window and define a canary ramp (suggested 10% -> 50% -> 100%)? What's the expected lead time?
- Naomi: CS/region — can you own monitoring and SLO alerts during the window and coordinate post-launch QA?

Attachments: brightware_q3_launch_forecast_v2.xlsx (forecast by cohort/timezone).

Goal: align on a concrete rollout plan by EOD Fri (Feb 13) so procurement can get the addendum ready. If helpful, proposing a 30-minute ops sync Thurs 2/12 11:00 PT — I can send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Tessa
--
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0112

From: Alice Park <alice.park@brightware.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, launchops@brightware.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Brightware Q3 launch — cohort lift quota handshake & forecast

Thanks Tessa — attaching a short note to clarify the forecast (we also shared an internal traffic profile). Key clarifications:

- The 2.5x spike is concentrated in a 3-hour window on peak launch day; most other periods will be aligned to ~1.1x baseline.
- Average token length per request ~180 tokens; 8% of requests will include embedding calls (those are batched separately).
- We will send a Canary traffic flag to Redwood's headers (x-brightware-cohort: true) for the first 48h.

About fallback: we are fine with an automatic model downgrade if latency > 600ms P95 for more than 5 minutes, but we'd like the option to force a manual rollback.

We need an answer on the temporary SLA/credits question for sustained 2.5x peaks — our procurement team asked if there is a standard addendum for rate windows.

Alice Park
Launch Lead, Brightware
alice.park@brightware.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Park <alice.park@brightware.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Brightware Q3 launch — cohort lift quota handshake & forecast

On Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 08:12 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the call yesterday...

Thanks for the details, Tessa / Alice. A few technical clarifications so we can size the temporary entitlement and recommend the fallback profile:

1) Request shape: are the 3-hour peak windows mostly short requests (few top-k tokens) or long chats with multi-turn context? The 180-token average is helpful; distribution tails matter for GPU memory pressure.
2) Embeddings: are embedding calls synchronous in the same user request path or sent as separate batch jobs? If synchronous, we need to carve a separate quota path or risk head-of-line blocking.
3) KV cache behavior: we should enable prefix KV caching for the cohort and set a 20-minute cache TTL to optimize cold-starts. That will reduce sustained token compute by ~18% based on similar launches.

Fallback recommendation: use the "redwood-medium-quant" variant as the automatic fallback for latency degradation (preserves semantic quality while saving ~30% per-token compute). For critical customer flows that require deterministic quality, keep a manual override button in the Console for Brightware's ops.

I will update the linked drive doc with sizing assumptions (see link in metadata). For the 2.5x short peak, if embeddings are synchronous we should require a separate embeddings entitlement; otherwise we can increase the text-gen quota by 2.5x for the 72-hour window.

Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Model Serving
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Park <alice.park@brightware.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 07:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Brightware Q3 launch — cohort lift quota handshake & forecast

Quick ops plan based on the asks and Karthik's notes:

- Lead time: we can provision a temporary rate window within 48 hours after procurement signs the addendum.
- Canary plan: 10% traffic for 24h (health checks + data integrity), 50% for next 24h, then 100% ramp if P95 latency < 500ms and error rate < 0.5%. We'll block auto-ramp if any of the conditions fail.
- Fallback routing: implement automatic downgrade to redwood-medium-quant variant when latency > 600ms P95 for 5 continuous minutes; manual rollback allowed by Brightware via the Console.
- Embeddings: we'll carve a separate embeddings queue if Brightware confirms synchronous usage; Marcus -> ops will need the exact header key for partitioning.

Attachments: quota-playbook.pdf (playbook + rollback runbook).

I'll prepare a short runbook and calendar the Thurs sync (Tessa if you send invite I will join with on-call).

Marcus Lin
Infrastructure & Reliability
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Perfect — thanks Marcus and Karthik. Action items:

- Naomi: please standby to create the monitoring dashboard and set the PagerDuty escalation policy for the launch window.
- Legal/Procurement: please draft the temp rate addendum (I'm attaching a starter draft: temp_rate_addendum_draft.docx). We need sign-off no later than Feb 19 to make the provisioning window.
- Marcus: please include the exact header name you will use for the embeddings carve in the runbook.

I'll host the 30-min sync in 30 minutes (invite sent). Alice — can you confirm if Brightware's embeddings are synchronous within the same request path (yes/no)? That will lock the entitlement approach.

Thanks — Tessa
